title: Actions
summary: Define mutations beside the route, submit to its URL, and let the router refresh the page data.

sections.title: Choose where the action runs
sections.body: clientAction executes in the browser. It can call your API, write browser storage, or perform another client operation. With the Vite server-route integration, action stays on the server and the browser calls it through the transport. Both exports may exist on one route. A clientAction takes precedence in the browser and decides whether to call serverAction. SSR does not execute clientAction.

sections.title: Start with a complete client action
sections.body: This settings example stores a display name in the browser. The handler receives a Request, decoded route params, and an AbortSignal. Read the submitted fields with request.formData(). A validation failure is ordinary returned data so the form can show it without replacing the entire route.

sections.title: Read the saved value
sections.body: The loader owns the saved value displayed by the page. After a successful action, the router runs the active page loader again unless shouldRevalidate opts out. Returning a validation object also counts as a completed action; use shouldRevalidate if that result should skip the read.

sections.title: Export the route module
sections.body: Keep the handler implementations in their own files. In file-router mode, routes/settings/route.ts maps to /settings. In manual mode, associate this same module with an explicit path in your route table.

sections.title: Register the actual URL
sections.body: The form targets /settings because that path is registered here. A fetcher is a route client: an arbitrary API URL without a matching route is not a substitute for registration. For Preact, change the framework imports in these examples to @kasperrt/smolter/preact.

sections.title: Submit and display the result
sections.body: The fetcher owns the submission result, pending state, and unexpected error. The page loader owns the saved name. The URL stays /settings during this submission, and the document is not reloaded. This deliberately uses ordinary HTML so the data flow is visible without a UI library.

sections.title: Navigation submissions
sections.body: Use Form when completing the mutation should commit navigation to the target route. Its result is read with useActionData. useActionData does not receive fetcher submissions: those belong to the fetcher that made them.

sections.title: POST, PUT, PATCH, and DELETE
sections.body: Every mutation method reaches the action on the matching route. Dispatch on request.method when one route supports several operations. Form method values are lowercase; imperative submit options use uppercase. The application defines what each method does; smolter does not infer database operations.

sections.title: Multiple intents on one route
sections.body: Named submit buttons contribute the selected button value to FormData. An intent is useful when multiple operations share the same HTTP method. Validate the intent in the action before writing anything.
sections.code:
<fetcher.Form action="/tasks/42" method="post">
  <button name="intent" value="complete">Complete</button>
  <button name="intent" value="reopen">Reopen</button>
</fetcher.Form>

// In the action:
const form = await request.formData();
const intent = form.get("intent");

if (intent !== "complete" && intent !== "reopen") {
  return new Error("Unknown task intent");
}

return tasks.setCompleted(params.id, intent === "complete");

sections.title: Implement the server action
sections.body: For server-backed settings, replace the localStorage implementation with a server action. The settings service below represents your application’s authenticated persistence layer: it must identify the user from the request and authorize the write. Its saveForRequest method returns the persisted settings or an Error. The Vite plugin removes this named server re-export from the browser module. Manually configured applications must use serverRoute in the browser and handleRequest on the server; merely naming a function action does not create an HTTP endpoint.

sections.title: Server action and client action together
sections.body: With the Vite plugin, re-export action from its server implementation file and clientAction from a browser-safe file. The client wrapper may inspect the form and then call serverAction. The transport preserves a copy of the request body for that call. Import the server handler only as a type in browser code; never import your database implementation there.

sections.title: Redirect after a mutation
sections.body: Return a Response with a Location header to navigate after saving. A redirect also navigates when the submission came from a fetcher. Use an internal destination registered in the router. There is no smolter redirect helper to import.

sections.title: Failures and cancellation
sections.body: Return an Error for an operation failure, rather than a field validation result. Fetcher failures appear in fetcher.error; navigation failures can render the route ErrorBoundary. Pass signal to fetch calls in client handlers. Aborting a request prevents stale UI results but cannot undo a mutation already accepted by a server. Enforce authorization and write consistency in your backend.

sections.title: Skip reads after validation failures
sections.body: Put shouldRevalidate beside the route and re-export it from the route module. The action result is unknown because the active page may be refreshed by a different route’s action. Narrow it before inspecting fields. Returning false retains the currently loaded page data; it does not cancel the action, suppress errors, or reload independent fetchers.
